description: Referenceable checklist of open work pulled from AI_HANDOFF.md, FEEL_AUDIT.md's Batch B/C backlog, and BUILDLOG.md's gamepad plan. Not a replacement for those files — this exists so nothing in the current open set gets silently dropped across sessions/tools. Tick items off by flipping status to 'done' and adding resolved_note + resolved_commit; keep finished items in the file for the record rather than deleting them.

tasks.title: Bind painted limb anchors to one authoritative bone graph
tasks.owner: Claude or Codex (implement), Derek (visual approval + Phase C go-ahead)
tasks.detail: Replace the remaining display-box/pivot approximation with an incremental two-anchor skin binding. Each textured limb maps its painted proximal and distal anchors onto shared bone joints; torso sockets own shoulders, hips, and neck; constraints modify bones rather than sprite X/Y. Preserve the current Phaser renderer, artwork, gameplay, and draw ordering.
tasks.next_step: Both characters' elbows done (George commit c8f8fae, Derek-approved in-browser; Thesz same session, same distalAnchorFrac mechanism). Knees investigated and found NOT to need the same fix -- see AI_HANDOFF.md's 2026-07-25 'knees investigated' entry: thighs are authored with deliberate overlap slack (unlike the flush-ending upper arm), so a dense ink-gap sweep (the metric that actually applies to that authoring style) already passes at 0.00px across the full angle range, both characters, both facings; a per-row anchor search confirmed there's no single flush row to bind to even at best fit (3.4-10px). No code change made for knees. Stopped per the blueprint's own guardrail before Phase C (torso sockets), which is a bigger structural step (retiring SHOULDER_STAGGER/HIP_STAGGER/etc. in favor of socket-rooted limbs) -- waiting on Derek's go-ahead before starting it.

tasks.title: Research better character movement and scalable moveset authoring
tasks.detail: Create a stack-specific reference covering articulated cutout movement, FK/IK constraints, painted-art anchors, animation timing/events, move data architecture, tooling/plugins, verification, and the tradeoffs of an external skeletal runtime.
tasks.resolved_note: Added CHARACTER_ANIMATION_AND_MOVESET_GUIDE.md and companion ANIMATION_TOOLING_AND_PLUGIN_EVALUATION.md using the installed Phaser 4.1/Vite/JavaScript rig and current primary documentation. Recommends retaining the custom rig, then adding local-space bone/anchor metadata, a small in-repo Phaser MoveRuntimePlugin with seekable clips/event markers/paired tracks, a central MoveSpec registry, and constraint/audit coverage. Phaser Editor, TexturePacker, and Spine are scoped future evaluations; Rex FSM is optional only as a narrow import; ContainerLite migration and Rive are not recommended for the current wrestler rig.

tasks.title: Codex: write the four input-invoked move blueprint
tasks.detail: Codex delivered the four era-appropriate moves: hammerlock (behind-the-back arm lock), rising knee lift, back body drop, and knee drop. Each has exactly four full POSES-format attacker poses, four MOVE_DEFS steps, a human-input trigger using existing controls, current-rig defender handling, tuning numbers, kit assignments, and optional AI notes.
tasks.resolved_note: Derek approved all four moves, the three directional-input overrides, the kit assignments, and the current-rig hammerlock approximation as proposed -- no rename, no scope changes. Claude implemented all four in Wrestler.js/Arena.js/AIHandler.js, added tools/debug/play.mjs coverage (hammerlock/kneeLift/backBodyDrop/kneeDrop scenarios), and fixed a pre-existing bug found along the way: Arena._orphanWatchdog's 0.6s grace period was silently cutting armBar/ankleLock/hammerlock's fixed-duration holds short (~1000ms early, skipping their release-drain bonus) because those holds release via a plain Wrestler-internal delayedCall rather than an Arena-tracked state; fixed with a new per-wrestler _fixedHold exemption flag. backBodyDrop AI deliberately left unwired per the blueprint's own note. Verified: npm test 43/43, npm run debug:play -- all 16/16, npm run build clean (Node 22.23.1 via nvm -- the shell default node v19.8.1 is below this project's >=20.19 floor). Full writeup in AI_HANDOFF.md's 2026-07-24 'four-move blueprint implemented and verified' entry. MOVES.md's move tables were already stale before this session (pre-dates suplex/headlock/armDrag/armBar/ankleLock/doubleAxeHandle/George) and were not touched -- flagged as a follow-up for whoever next does a docs pass.

tasks.title: Fix per-character leg/shin tilts to mirror with facing (knee detaches on turn)
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md, Codex entry 2026-07-14 'knee connections break on facing changes'
tasks.detail: Skeleton.updateUpright's per-character _nearLegTilt/_nearShinTilt/_farLegTilt were screen-absolute while the true thighAng/shinAng bone chain mirrors with facing, so a knee tuned correctly in one facing detached in the other -- reproducible in the rig-tuner and in-game on turn. Both George and Thesz were affected.
tasks.resolved_note: Multiplied all three tilts by `facing` in Skeleton.js's updateUpright; `_farLegTilt` now also goes through the mirror it used to bypass when set. Existing tuned values are a no-op at facing=+1 (the tuning convention) and only change the previously-broken facing=-1 case. Verified: npm test 43/43, debug:play -- all 12/12, build clean, rig-tuner smoke.mjs 16/16, plus visual screenshots of both characters in both facings. Did NOT build the rig-tuner facing-toggle parity smoke check Codex's review suggested -- see rig-tuner-facing-parity-check below, split out as its own follow-up.

tasks.title: Add a rig-tuner facing-toggle parity smoke check
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md, Codex entry 2026-07-14 'knee connections break on facing changes' -- 'Add a rig-tuner smoke/parity check that toggles facing and compares the reflected transforms'
tasks.detail: Split out from mirrored-knee-tilt-fix, which fixed the underlying bug but verified it manually (screenshots) rather than adding an automated regression check. Would toggle facing in the rig-tuner harness and assert hip/knee/shin origins and rotations reflect across the wrestler centerline for both George and Thesz.
tasks.next_step: Partially covered as a side effect of tools/debug/knee_pivot_audit.mjs (2026-07-15, see knee-pivot-structural-fix) -- it confirmed facing-symmetric distances at matching gait phases across both P1/P2 slots, but that's a byproduct of a different script, not a dedicated rig-tuner-integrated parity check. Still not started as its own thing.

tasks.title: Carry the child-joint attachment contract through shoulders, elbows, hips, and knees
tasks.detail: George's arm still detached, and the first shared-shoulder attempt then distorted both wrestlers' silhouettes. The durable contract must preserve authored shoulder silhouettes, keep internal child pivots on the true joint through rotation, account for near/far render scale, and be verifiable against painted pixels rather than display rectangles. It applies to George, Lou Thesz, placeholders, and future wrestlers in upright and grounded/get-up rendering.
tasks.resolved_note: Supersedes the first 2026-07-24 SHOULDER_OVERLAP implementation. Upper arms now stay at the authored shoulder (no football-pad backoff); fallback forearms overlap along the child angle; far elbow endpoints use the same 0.85 depth scale as their rendered art. Removed George's pose-dependent screen-space forearm offsets so his existing internal pivot metadata stays on the true elbow. The cutter now preserves authored overlap for Thesz forearm/shin, and thesz.js records their measured jointPivotFrac values; the shin returned to its authored 51x95 box. A follow-up angle sweep exposed a remaining presentation defect: the derived forearm formula changed relative angle during shoulder travel and the child overlap drew over the upper-arm cap. The default is now a stable 0.70-rad elbow hinge, with upper-arm caps drawn just above forearm overlap inside the existing depth bands. The audit now samples real PNG alpha around every true neck/shoulder/elbow/hip/knee, not just render boxes. It passes both wrestlers, both facings, six extreme upright poses, and four get-up samples with 0px maximum painted gap. Full verification is recorded in AI_HANDOFF.md's 2026-07-25 correction entries.

tasks.title: Seat Gorgeous George's painted boot soles on the mat
tasks.detail: George visibly floated even though the procedural ankle targets were planted, because mathematical foot points did not account for the transformed alpha extent of his baked boot art. The far sole measured 6.6-13.5 screen px above the mat across idle/walking samples.
tasks.resolved_note: Corrected george.js farShinOffsetY from -12 to 2. The old negative value moved the reduced 0.77-scale far shin upward, opposite its comment's intended ground correction. Alpha-aware world-space measurements now put the far sole within -2.4px to +2.4px of the mat in planted walking frames; both idle soles are within 2-4.5px in both facings. George's knee chain still passes the painted-pixel attachment audit at 0px separation.

tasks.title: Art/cutter decision: remove the zero-margin knee-seam problem at the source
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md, Claude entry 2026-07-14 'first live tuning session'
tasks.detail: The knee cap currently tucks with zero margin against the thigh's closed dark outline -- any future shin-down nudge re-exposes the seam. Two options parked for Derek: unlined overlap zone on the thigh's knee end, or a soft-faded shin cap (drawn or as a cutter post-processing step). Either removes the zero-margin fragility entirely instead of re-tuning around it every session.
tasks.next_step: First attempt (Sprite sheets/newLegLou/, 2026-07-15) tested through the real cutter pipeline; initial diagnosis (an ink line intruding into the shin's cap region) was WRONG -- Derek correctly suspected a pivot-crop mismatch instead. Confirmed: the cutter's pivotCrop step centers each part on its own top-row ink center, and the new thigh's pivot delta measured 21px different (source-canvas terms) from the working thigh's while the shin barely moved. Proven by test: re-applying the new art (ink line untouched) with legOffsetX nudged -15->-9 to compensate made the notch disappear completely. So any thigh redraw will need an offset retune regardless of art cleanliness -- the pivot is derived from ink shape, not a fixed marker. Nothing adopted yet -- reverted after the diagnostic test. Superseded by knee-pivot-structural-fix below: don't redraw or retune until that decision is made, since a redraw alone won't survive pose changes without the structural fix too.

tasks.title: Re-cut/re-pad Thesz's thigh.png so its knee anchor centers (Codex's decision)
tasks.owner: Derek (approve the crop operation), then Claude executes
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md 2026-07-15 'knee audit' entry + Codex's 2026-07-15 decision entry + Claude's reply
tasks.detail: Proved, not just suspected: the skeleton's true knee joint, the shin's render origin, and the artwork's own intended knee point do not stay coincident across poses (see the 2026-07-15 'knee audit' entry for full numbers -- thigh art-implied knee point drifts 5.4-15.8px near / 11.8-20.1px far across one walk cycle; thigh-vs-shin art gap swings 3.7-14.7px near / 3.9-19.9px far, a 4-5x range). Codex decided the direction: repair the asset (thigh.png is 22.3% of its canvas width off-center at the knee edge; shin is only 0.3% off, essentially fine), not the runtime rig -- a rig-side rotating correction would bake a crop accident into permanent per-character metadata and risk pushing the mismatch to the ankle/boot instead. Explicit acceptance criteria set: preserve visible ink/scale/vertical extent, change only transparent padding/crop; bottom-edge knee center within 1% of canvas width from center; thigh-vs-shin art-knee separation <=3px through idle + the sampled walk cycle, both facings, per tools/debug/knee_pivot_audit.mjs; do NOT retune legOffsetX/shin offsets/pose angles as a workaround before re-running the audit, since that would mask whether the crop fix worked; if the 3px bound can't be hit with a centered asset while preserving ink, stop and report back rather than forcing it -- fallback in that case is explicit normalized joint-anchor metadata, not more fixed nudges.
tasks.next_step: Waiting on Derek's approval of the transparent-padding/crop operation itself (nothing executed yet). Once approved: Claude re-pads thigh.png (ink/scale/extent unchanged, crop/padding only), reruns tools/debug/knee_pivot_audit.mjs thesz to confirm the acceptance numbers, runs the full verification suite, then Derek does the in-browser visual sign-off.

tasks.title: Replace scissor-walk gait with a natural 4-phase walk + proximity-based wrestling shuffle
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md, Codex entry 2026-07-14 'locomotion direction: replace scissor walk'
tasks.detail: Current open-ring walk reads as two straight legs scissoring through one hinge. Approved direction: open-ring gets a real 4-phase walk (contact / weight acceptance / bent-knee pass / extension) with the swing leg folding underneath the body; close range gets a guarded shorter wrestling shuffle (lead/rear stance, soft knees, small foot travel, no big centerline crossing); running/whip locomotion stays untouched. Blend lower-body gait intent through the existing combatBlend proximity seam rather than adding a new distance state; each leg adopts new gait params only during its own swing/footfall transition, not mid-plant (avoids skating).
tasks.next_step: mirrored-knee-tilt-fix is done; still blocked on lou-knee-art-cleanup landing first (per Codex's explicit recommended order) so the new gait isn't tuned against an art/rig bug that's about to change. Verification plan already specified: instrument planted-foot slip, capture both facings at contact/passing/extension, cross the full combatBlend range without pops, test stop/reverse/diagonal/crouched-close-range/entry-into-running, require Derek's playtest.

tasks.title: Decide whether distinct near/far leg texture keys are still needed
tasks.detail: Potential later art support: nearThigh/nearShin + farThigh/farShin textures (falling back to today's shared thigh/shin) as perspective/depth variants using the same joint conventions -- explicitly NOT to be scoped until the new gait silhouettes exist, otherwise Derek draws final art against motion that's about to change.
tasks.next_step: Do not start until natural-walk-shuffle-prototype has a signed-off silhouette.

tasks.title: George's final full-body/limb art pass + fresh rig tuning
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md, Codex entry 2026-07-14 'locomotion direction', recommended-order step 5
tasks.detail: Originally planned as the last step of the locomotion/art sequence because old George offsets and display boxes were fitted to stretched art. Derek later supplied the NewGeorge redraw and live-directed the replacement/tuning work before the earlier gait sequence completed.
tasks.resolved_note: The NewGeorge full-body reference was cut into six layers, wired into the current skeleton, recalibrated for real-world height, given explicit knee/elbow attachment pivots, and live-tuned with Derek across multiple July 19-23 sessions. The remaining dark-ear concern is isolated as george-ear-art-touchup rather than keeping the completed redraw/rig pass blocked.

tasks.title: Thin George's dark inner-ear shading at game scale
tasks.owner: Derek (approve art edit), then Claude or Codex executes
tasks.detail: The blanket cutter gap-close bug was fixed and scoped to George's shin, but the ear still reads as a black patch at game scale. Direct sampling showed the dark canal fill already exists in the raw GeorgeHead.png source; grayscale plus the small rendered head makes it merge visually. Codex recommends a localized source-art touch-up rather than changing headScale or adding another general cutter heuristic.
tasks.next_step: Derek approves a localized thinning/lightening of the inner-ear canal shading in the source art. Re-cut only the head, compare at actual in-game scale in both facings, then run the normal verification suite.

tasks.title: Hard horizontal knee seam still visible in parts of the walking stride
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md, Codex entry 2026-07-14 'knee connections break on facing changes', closing note
tasks.detail: Distinct from the facing-mirroring bug above: Codex's live four-frame game check still showed the cap seam mid-stride even accounting for facing. Derek's planned art cleanup on the closed knee outline/cap addresses this; related to but not solved by lou-knee-art-cleanup or mirrored-knee-tilt-fix alone.
tasks.next_step: Runtime geometry now passes the 2026-07-24 all-joint audit with at least 1.8px coverage across both facings and sampled poses. This item remains open only for the separate visible ink/cap seam: Derek reviews the walking knee in-browser and, if the line remains visible, handles it as source-art/crop cleanup rather than another runtime offset.

tasks.owner: Claude (implement), gated on Derek prioritizing it
tasks.detail: Five deferred improvements, all agreed on by Claude's reply: (1) overlay true neck/shoulder/elbow/hip/knee/ankle joints, (2) draw a line from each true joint to its rendered texture origin, (3) compact comparison grid for both facings x idle/stride-extremes/crouch/a move pose, (4) encode or warn on known coupled values (overlap vs display-box height, bone length vs box height, Thesz near/far leg lockstep), (5) warn when a visually-joined seam's true joint displacement exceeds a small threshold -- this one would have caught the knee-cleave regression automatically and is the one to promote first.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT B2 -- contact-time hitstop and impact feedback
tasks.source: FEEL_AUDIT.md Batch B; AI_HANDOFF.md multiple entries name this as 'next per the brief's sequence'
tasks.detail: No hitstop exists anywhere; jab/headbutt have zero contact feedback. Add a small Arena-owned gameplay hitstop timer that gates _tickGame dt (ts-safe): jab ~35-45ms, headbutt/clothesline ~55-75ms, major landings ~80-110ms. Move knockdown camera shake from fall-complete to the actual contact frame; add a small shake to jab/headbutt.
tasks.next_step: Next in the core-feel-trio sequence after B1 (done) -- B2, then B3, per Codex's explicit brief.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT B3 -- gravity-correct knockdown fall arcs
tasks.detail: Falls currently rise fast (83ms) and float down slowly (284ms) -- anti-gravity, 1:3.4 rise:fall ratio measured. Replace with a two-phase arc: ~35-45% duration accelerating-ease-out rise, ~55-65% accelerating-ease-in descent, landing at speed, horizontal travel finishing at or just before touchdown. Preserve all existing ring clamps (Batch A).
tasks.next_step: Third of the core feel trio, after B1 (done) and B2.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT B4 -- momentum-scaled knockback
tasks.detail: Knockback distance should scale with victim speed at contact (standing x1, whipped runner x~2); rebound clothesline/axe-handle drain x1.4 on running victims. Currently momentum isn't conserved and running hits no harder than standing hits.
tasks.next_step: After the B1-B3 core trio lands and is re-measured; implement after B2/B3 per Codex's sequencing note ('implement after the basic velocity and fall models stabilize').

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT B5 -- rope rebound loads the body
tasks.detail: Rope rebound is currently an instant velocity flip. Add an 80-100ms hold/compress at the rope plane (existing rope-sag visual spike plays) before reversal.
tasks.next_step: Same sequencing tier as B4/B6 -- after the core trio.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT B6 -- per-wrestler mass
tasks.detail: One mass scalar per PRESETS entry (george 0.92, brawler 1.0, thesz 1.12): walk/run speed divided by mass, received knockback divided by mass, bump/get-up duration multiplied by mass, whip-run speed divided by mass. Currently all three body types share one physical body.
tasks.next_step: Same sequencing tier as B4/B5 -- after the core trio. Touches several interconnected systems, do last within Batch B per Codex's note.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT C1 -- kickout depth tracks damage
tasks.source: FEEL_AUDIT.md Batch C; confirmed still untouched by the 2026-07-11 post-Thesz-press baseline (91-100% count-1 kickouts across both matchups)
tasks.detail: Replace the binary first-press-escape with a continuous per-press success curve so covers on a 70-stamina wrestler break at 1, 40-stamina at 2, 20-stamina at 2.7+ -- while fresh wrestlers never die to a cheap cover. Currently 91-100% of kickouts happen at count 1 with zero nearfalls in most matchups.
tasks.next_step: Derek owns the booking-tuning call (thresholds/curve shape); Claude implements once direction is set. C1 is one of the two 'drama pair' items Codex called out as highest priority within Batch C.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT C2 -- kill the zombie phase / redesign finish-hunting
tasks.source: FEEL_AUDIT.md Batch C + the 2026-07-11 post-Thesz-press baseline finding
tasks.detail: Original C2 design (AI hunts the finish once opponent's standing stamina drops below ~15) is confirmed dead on arrival: George is standing below 60 stamina in 0.3% of trace samples and below 42 in 0.0% -- the 'standing opponent below threshold' state the finishers gate on essentially never occurs, because taunt regen (~35/match) and kickout refunds lift him back over every threshold before he's upright. Must instead catch the down/getting-up window directly, or suppress the recovery stack (taunt conversion + kickout refunds) once a wrestler has been driven under the threshold, or both.
tasks.next_step: Derek weighs in on the redesigned trigger (down-window vs. recovery-stack suppression vs. both) -- explicitly flagged in the handoff as needing his input before implementation.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT C3 -- escalation gates on big moves + diminishing repetition heat
tasks.detail: AI shouldn't throw piledriver/sleeper/top-tier moves before damage+heat justify them (e.g. piledriver odds ~0 until opponent <55 stamina or heat >45, ramping after); pair with per-move diminishing heat (bump x 0.65^(uses in last 60s)) so spamming a move stops paying. Currently finishers can open a match at 0:05 and repeat up to 35 times with no penalty.
tasks.next_step: After C1/C2 land and are re-measured, per Codex's stated order.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT C4 -- fights use the ring (recenter after wall knockdowns)
tasks.detail: After downing an opponent at the ropes, AI should reposition to the open side; slams/whips delivered at a wall should aim the throw toward ring center. A1 (already shipped) restored the whip counter, which does part of this job already.
tasks.next_step: After C1-C3, per Codex's stated order.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT C5 -- damage shows in movement/attack speed
tasks.detail: Scale whip/self-run speed and attack pose-sequence durations by stamina (full speed at 100, ~70% at 0), keeping impact-callback timing proportional, so a beaten wrestler reads beaten in every action, not just get-ups.
tasks.next_step: After C1-C4, per Codex's stated order.

tasks.title: FEEL_AUDIT C6 -- AI learns the rest of its kit
tasks.detail: Give the AI suplex + armDrag from lockup, occasional turnbuckle dives when the opponent is down mid-ring at high heat, and possum for George -- personality-specific use of mechanics already available to humans (George = theater, Thesz = sport, brawler = direct force). Explicitly last in the C-batch sequence.
tasks.next_step: Only after C1-C5 land, per Codex's stated order and the project's own priority (psychology/drama over flash).

tasks.title: Wire up gamepad support (mapping exists, never connected to Arena)
tasks.source: BUILDLOG.md 'NEXT SESSION: gamepad support' entry; confirmed still true via MOVES.md:15 and PRD.md:205
tasks.detail: input.gamepad plugin is enabled and InputHandler.js already has a full gamepad branch (A=grapple, B=run, X=power, Y=finisher, LB=evade, RB=block, d-pad + left stick 0.4 deadzone) -- but Arena never constructs a 'gamepad' InputHandler, so none of it has ever executed. Six-step plan already written: (1) verify actual Phaser 4 gamepad Button API (.pressed/.value, no built-in justDown -- needs per-frame edge detection), (2) press-any-button pad assignment (pad0 -> current keyboard player, pad1 -> the other), (3) extend the 1/2 mode-toggle cycle to include a GAMEPAD state + handle disconnect, (4) unlock audio on first gamepad button press too, (5) real-controller playtest as the primary check, (6) optionally inject a fake navigator.getGamepads for headless debug:play coverage.
tasks.next_step: Not started. Flagged repeatedly as 'the strongest parallel product/accessibility task' that can run alongside the feel-batch work without touching the same systems.

tasks.detail: Many grounded, falling, grabbed, and complex-move states still draw with Graphics primitives instead of the textured six-part skeleton, which limits selling quality and leaves the PNG art integration incomplete.
tasks.next_step: Explicitly 'a later readability/polish project, not part of B1' -- no owner or timeline assigned yet.

tasks.title: Historical announcer commentary system -- 50-clip pilot
tasks.source: AI_HANDOFF.md, entry on pre-generated commentary audio (~line 780)
tasks.detail: Approved future direction, not implemented: pre-generated (not live-TTS) commentary clips, event/intensity/match-phase-tagged, fetched lazily post audio-unlock gesture (full 300-clip library as decoded Web Audio buffers would run ~250MB RAM), one active voice at a time with per-line/category cooldowns, ducked under the synthesized crowd. Data shape: stable ID, transcript, event type, intensity, valid match phases, wrestler/venue applicability, factual source/review status, cooldown, asset path. Recommended: ship a 50-clip pilot before scaling to the full ~300.
tasks.next_step: Explicitly deferred behind the B1/B2 feel work per the entry's own request. Revisit once the feel-batch and psychology-batch work above is further along.
